newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Deutsche's Breuer to succeed Kopper as CEO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Deutsche's Breuer to succeed Kopper as CEO.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Wednesday that management board member Rolf Breuer would succeed chief executive Hilmar Kopper next May to take on one of the most powerful posts in the German economy.

Continuing a rigorous management reorganisation launched earlier this year, Germany's largest bank said two other management board members, Ellen Schneider-Lenne and Ulrich Cartellieri would leave the management board and be replaced by the former president of Credit Suisse, Josef Ackermann.

Kopper, lambasted in the German media in 1994 for describing multi-million-mark losses from the collapse of the Schneider real estate empire as "peanuts," would be proposed for election to the supervisory board next spring, Deutsche said in a statement released after a supervisory board meeting.
The departure of Cartellieri and Schneider-Lenne was expected but analysts said the appointment of Breuer, 58, came as something of a surprise.

Breuer, a vocal and eloquent proponent of promoting equity culture in Germany, is one of three management board members in charge of investment banking and his appointment highlights the importance Deutsche places in that business, analysts said.
"From the point of view of the bank's strategic direction, its interest in being a worldwide investment bank, this is a logical step," said Dieter Hein, banking analyst at BHF-Bank.
Kopper had been chief executive since 1989 when his predecessor Alfred Herrhausen was murdered by terrorists.

He oversaw the bank's drive into investment banking with the acquisition of London-based Morgan Grenfell and the subsequent concentration of its investment banking business in London, a move seen as a blow to Frankfurt's standing as a financial centre.

"I think Kopper will take his role as supervisory board member very seriously," said Christine Winkler, banking analyst at Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG. "He is after all a banker through and through."
The statement said Kopper, Schneider-Lenne and Cartellieri would be leaving the management board at their own request.
"At its meeting today, the supervisory board complied with those requests," the statement said.

Ackermann, who until the middle of the year was president of the executive board of Swiss banking group Credit Suisse, would take over responsibility for credit risks from Schneider-Lenne at the end of the year and then, in spring 1997, the market risks, treasury and economics divisions from Cartellieri, the statement said.
